transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-21
Start time: 14:32 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Samira Khan (Redwood AE), Miguel Ortega (Redwood SE), Tara Bhattacharya (Equinox Head of ML), Ethan Cole (Equinox Infra), Marta Ruiz (Equinox Security)

Summary:
Quick Optimize walkthrough focused on quantization profiles (INT8 vs FP8), demonstration of Redwood Optimize recommendations and quality vs latency tradeoffs. Equinox is evaluating pilot for production chat + embedding pipeline; key constraints are latency < 120ms p50 for short prompts, cost target, and strict security (VPC, KMS, SOC2). Next steps: share benchmarks, pricing, and compliance docs; schedule pilot kickoff.

Topics covered:
- Overview of Redwood Optimize and quantization profiles
- INT8 vs FP8 quality vs latency and throughput numbers from demo
- Fallbacks and routing (hosted vs dedicated vs private)
- Security: VPC, KMS, audit logs, SOC2/ISO concerns
- Pilot scope, timeline and evaluation criteria

Action items (recap in call): see metadata list above

Transcript body:
[00:00] Samira Khan: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros, we got miguel from the se team who will run the demo, and then tara, ethan, marta from equinox?
[00:06] Tara Bhattacharya: yep, that's right. tara here, head of ml at equinox. thanks for doing this.
[00:09] Ethan Cole: ethan, infra. i set up the calendar links.
[00:11] Marta Ruiz: marta, security. i'll jump in on compliance questions.
[00:15] Miguel Ortega: good afternoon, all. im gonna share my screen, walk through optimize, quant profiles, and then we'll show INT8 and FP8 runs side-by-side. hope that's ok.
[00:28] Samira Khan: and just to set goals, tara said you want to validate quality drop is acceptable and whether we can meet latency SLOs while reducing cost. also confirm security posture for private deployment.
[00:36] Tara: correct. our main prompt lengths are 30-150 tokens, p50 latency target ~120 ms for short inference, and cost per 1k tokens needs to drop by at least 30% vs current baseline.
[00:47] Miguel: perfect. quick architecture note — for the demo i'm using a 16k context open model variant, we've prepared three quant profiles: fp16 baseline, int8 aggressive, and fp8 balanced. we're showing generation quality on our eval set of 200 prompts, plus latency histograms.
[01:05] Miguel: sharing screen now... forgive the garbled slide titles, sometimes the auto-export renames things — this is the Optimize console -> Quant Profiles tab.
[01:22] Miguel: first slide: fp16 baseline p50 = 95 ms, p95 = 210 ms (on our test rig), throughput ~18 tokens/sec. int8 aggressive p50 = 72 ms, p95 = 140 ms, throughput ~26 tokens/sec, but some quality delta on longer context completions. fp8 balanced p50 = 80 ms, p95 = 150 ms, throughput 24 tokens/sec, quality much closer to fp16.
[01:55] Tara: can you quantify the quality drop for int8? like rouge or BLEU or human eval?
[02:02] Miguel: sure — we ran automatic metrics and a small human eval. int8 had an average BLEU-like delta of -2.3 points and a human preference hit of ~12% vs fp16 for open-ended creative prompts; for structured completion tasks the gap was <5%. fp8 had delta about -0.7 BLEU and human preference ~4% — so much smaller.
[02:27] Ethan: those numbers look promising. our workload is mixed — a lot of summarization and retrieval-augmented generation for docs, so we care more about factual consistency. how did hallucination behave under int8?
[02:37] Miguel: good question — on RAG tasks int8 showed a small uptick in hallucination cases, mainly when context windows approach 8-12k and the tokenization boundaries hit quantized layers. fp8 was nearly indistinguishable from fp16 on RAG. we also have per-prompt quality flags in the console so you can see examples where quality regressed.
[02:58] Marta: on security, we need to know where keys live and audit logs. if we go private, can we manage KMS?
[03:05] Samira: yes — in Private mode customers can bring-your-own-kms (BYOK) and we support HSM-backed keys. we push audit logs to your S3/logging endpoint and you control retention. we'll share SOC2 and ISO attestations in the security packet.
[03:20] Marta: and RBAC? we need role separation between devs and ops.
[03:24] Miguel: console has RBAC with SAML SSO integration; you can map roles and restrict rollout controls. we also support per-route throttles and token-level cost tagging in the console.
[03:40] Ethan: about latency — those p50 numbers are on your bench. can we reproduce on our GCP/NV setups? we run A100-like hardware but with different seq length distribution.
[03:50] Miguel: absolutely — in the benchmark pack we'll share the raw traces and the kernel selection logs. you can re-run with your profile; Optimize will recommend a quant profile and batching settings tuned to your sequence length distribution. we can also run an on-prem benchmark during the pilot.
[04:07] Tara: timeline: we want to decide on vendor early January and run pilot in Jan. is that feasible?
[04:12] Samira: yes — pilot kickoff week of 2026-12-29 is possible but i think january week 1/2 also works. we can provision a dedicated pool for 30 days and run your evals.
[04:22] Miguel: quick demo clip: here's the side-by-side output for prompt id 1429 — fp16 vs int8 vs fp8. you can see the int8 output drops a couple of details, fp8 retains more factual tokens. (screen) the console highlights tokens with lower confidence in orange, so it's easy to triage which prompts need higher fidelity.
[04:55] Tara: is there an automated rollback or policy to route certain prompts to fp16 if confidence is low?
[05:01] Miguel: yes — you can set routing policies by confidence threshold, latency, or tag. for example, critical prompt routes can be pinned to fp16, or we can route to fp16 on fallback after a quantized variant times out.
[05:12] Ethan: what's the effort to integrate with our pipeline? we have k8s endpoints and an internal proxy.
[05:18] Samira: we have an API-first approach. you hit the Redwood API for generation; for Private you run the control plane in your VPC and the inference plane sits in your environment. we provide helm charts for k8s or a docker-based on-prem package. Miguel: we usually do a 2-week integration window during pilot to validate routing and keys.
[05:35] Miguel: small note — quantization profiles can be tuned per-model and per-route. you don't need a single global profile. Optimize will suggest per-route profiles based on traffic.
[05:46] Marta: auditability: can we get token-level logs for compliance? we need to show what prompts were sent and model versions used.
[05:54] Samira: yes we have token-level metadata and model versioning; logs include model sha, quant profile id, route id, and latency. we redact content if you request PII scrubbing.
[06:08] Tara: what about cost math? if int8 gives 30-40% CPU/GPU savings, does that map linearly to spend?
[06:15] Miguel: not perfectly linear — gains depend on batching and KV cache hit rates. in our tests int8 reduced GPU time ~35% on average which roughly translated to 30% lower per-token infra cost after amortizing overheads. fp8 was ~25% GPU time reduction with much smaller quality delta.
[06:35] Ethan: we are also considering dedicated capacity vs hosted. what's the SLA for Dedicated?
[06:40] Samira: dedicated has SLA-backed uptime and latency tiers; we can include that in the pilot contract. Hosted is faster to start but may have noisier tail latencies during peaks; Dedicated gives you isolated pools and predictable throughput.
[06:55] Miguel: also worth noting that you can start hosted for the pilot to iterate quickly, then move to dedicated or private when you sign a commitment. Optimize settings are consistent across modes.
[07:08] (discussion continues — demo shows more examples, a couple of awkward transcriptions)
[28:30] Miguel: jumping ahead — here's the benchmark CSV summary: int8 mean latency 78 ms, fp8 86 ms, fp16 96 ms p50 on the test rig; p95 tails are the main concern, int8 p95 was 160 ms vs fp8 150 ms vs fp16 210 ms.
[32:44] Tara: does Redwood do automated retraining or quant-aware finetuning to improve int8 fidelity?
[32:51] Miguel: we don't retrain customer models but Optimize supports quant-aware calibration passes and per-layer clipping heuristics; we can also run a short finetune step if you want to close the gap — that's in the services add-on.
[38:10] Marta: i need the SOC2 report and architecture diagram for our security review — can you send an engineers contact for deeper questions?
[38:17] Samira: yes, i'll attach the security packet and put miguel's contact for technical follow-ups.
[45:02] Miguel: final notes — when we run the pilot we'll provide an A/B harness, pre-baked eval sets, and the dashboard with per-prompt diffs. you'll be able to toggle profiles and see live traffic impact.
[47:20] Tara: looks good. assuming pricing is reasonable and security checks out, i think pilot in first week of january is greenlight.
[49:05] Samira: great — recap of next steps: we'll send pricing/pilot terms, benchmark artifacts, and security docs. ethan to confirm infra access, marta to compile compliance list.
[49:20] Ethan: i'll try to get the VPC peering details by end of week.
[49:24] Marta: i'll email the list to samira today.
[49:30] Samira: thanks everyone. we'll follow up with a calendar invite for the pilot kickoff.
[49:35] Tara: thanks, bye.

End of recording.
